newsitem.title: ITALY: San Paolo says won't take BankNapoli stake.
newsitem.headline: San Paolo says won't take BankNapoli stake.

text.p: Italian bank San Paolo di Torino does not intend to take any direct stake in troubled Banco di Napoli, 60 percent of which the Treasury has put up for sale, San Paolo chairman Gianni Zandano said.
Three Italian groups, including BNL and insurer INA, and three foreign institutions, have expressed an interest in the bank. Other names have not been released.

Zandano told reporters after an INA board meeting to discuss the stake issue, " Our contribution will not involve a direct intervention even though it is in our interest and that of the banking system to assure the equity balance of Banco di Napoli."
San Paolo's contribution, Zandano said, would be limited to "advice and suggestions."
Interested parties have until December 20 to make offers for the majority stake in the struggling Naples bank.
